previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, steroid dependence, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for hypotension and recurrent falls following a reduction in prednisone dose. He presented with systolic blood pressure as low as 70, requiring vasopressor support and ICU admission. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury likely due to hypovolemia, negative head and neck imaging after trauma from falls, and no evidence of sepsis or acute cardiac event. Adrenal insufficiency was considered a contributing factor. He was treated with stress-dose hydrocortisone, fluid resuscitation, and vasopressors, which were successfully weaned. His blood pressure stabilized, renal function improved, and he was transitioned to 10 mg daily oral prednisone with a rescue dexamethasone dose for home use. Other medications were adjusted, including reduction of carvedilol and temporary hold of spironolactone, with torsemide restarted at 50 mg daily. He developed a diarrhea episode consistent with IBS, which resolved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans across multiple specialties.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ YOM with obesity, IDDM, and psoriatic 
arthritis c/b steroid dependence and relative adrenal 
insufficiency with recent admission for hypotension, discharged 
recently with rescue dose dexamethasone, who presents with a 
similar episode because he could not fill his rescue 
dexamethasone dose. 

# Hypotension: this is ___ episode of hypotension at home, very 
similar to past presentation. This time, perhaps it was 
triggered by his IBD flare and diarrhea. In the past, these 
episodes of hypotension were thought to be ___ adrenal 
insufficiency, and pt reports on admission that these episodes 
happen when his prednisone is dropped below 20 mg/day. His BP 
improved in ED after 1 L IVF in ED and 10 mg IV dexa. Less 
likely to be due to volume depletion this time, as patient was 
not orthostatic on the floor. His SBP on the floor remained in 
range of 110-120s, and he was restarted on coreg 6.25 mg BID and 
torsemide 50 mg QD. It is not likely triggered by infection as 
pt remained afebrile during the stay w/o any symptoms of 
infection. UCx was negative and BCx are pending without growth 
to date. Endocrine was curb-sided for alternative rescue 
medication and patient was prescribed hydrocortisone 100 mg/2mL 
and his prednisone was increased to 20 mg daily. He will follow 
up with Dr. ___. 
  
# Hypokalemia: Likely from diarrhea losses vs stopping 
spironolactone. He presented with K of 2.7 and was repleted in 
ED with 40 mEq IV and 40 mEq PO. His potassium increased to 4.6. 
His potassium was monitored with additional doses of torsemide 
and repleted as needed. He will be discharged with liquid 
potassium chloride as solid forms of potassium chloride 
interacts with anticholinergics and increase risk of gastric 
bleeding. He is being discharged with outpatient lab orders to 
check potassium and creatinine with the arrangement that his lab 
results will be faxed to his PCP. 
  
# Diarrhea: Prior to admission, pt was having ___ BM a day with 
cramping, c/w previous IBD flares. He reports he has been on 
steroids so long that GI doctors have not ___ able to biopsy 
him for diagnosis of type. Family history of both UC and 
crohn's. He was continued on azathioprine, prednisone and was 
symptomatically managed on phenobarb-hyoscy-atropine-scopolamine 
and imodium. His c diff toxin was negative on ___. His diarrhea 
slowed down to 3 BM/day by the time of discharge.
  
# Anemia: Hct 36 which is at pt baseline. Could be due to 
myelosupression from azathioprine or could be from chronic 
disease. He was continued on ferrous sulfate. 
  
# Diabetes: On determir at home. He was recently seen by ___ 
during last admission and his long acting insulin was adjusted. 
He carb counts before meals and calculates his humalog dose. 
Continued on insulin lantus 20 units in AM, 29 units in ___ and 
carb counting with diabetic diet.
  
# Lower extremity edema: thought to be from prednisone. Treated 
with torsemide and spironolactone prior to previous admission. 
During the last admission, spironolactone was stopped due to 
concern about anti-androgenic side effects and also about 
anti-aldosterone effects with worsening hypotension. When his 
blood pressure normalized, he was restarted on 50 mg daily of 
torsemide with good urine output. His potassium was monitored 
and repleted as needed with torsemide use. He also had ACE 
bandage wrap to help with his lower extremity edema.

# Psoriatic arthritis: Patient gets Stelara every 3 months for 
control of his joint pain in addition to azathioprine and 
prednisone. He is due for injection in about a week and is 
feeling the increased joint pain. He was continued on lidocaine 
patches with some relief of pain, and was also started on PO 
morphine prn which helped. He will follow up with Dr. ___ on 
___ in pain clinic for Stelara injection.
  
# Peripheral neuropathy: He was continued on home doses of 
nortriptyline, pregabalin, tizanidine for his peripheral 
neuropathy.
  
# OSA: he was continued on home CPAP.
